---
title: Maximal m-step solvable quotient
kind: definition
summary: 'For a profinite group $G$, the quotient $G^m = G/G[m]$ by the $m$-th closed derived subgroup. For a field $K$, $G_K^m$ is the Galois group of the maximal $m$-step solvable extension $K_m/K$.'
tags: [galois-groups, solvable-quotients]
---

**Definition.** Let $G$ be a profinite group. Put $G[0] = G$ and let $G[i+1] = [G[i], G[i]]$ be the closed subgroup generated by commutators. The maximal $i$-step solvable quotient is $G^i = G/G[i]$. So $G^1$ is the abelianization and $G^2$ is the maximal metabelian quotient. The maximal prosolvable quotient is $G^{\mathrm{sol}} = G / \bigcap_i G[i]$, the inverse limit of the $G^i$ [@saiditamagawa2022, §0, Notations].

For a field $K$, write $G_K^m$ for this quotient of the absolute Galois group and $K_m/K$ for the corresponding extension, so $\mathrm{Gal}(K_m/K) = G_K^m$ [@saiditamagawa2022, §0].

**Warning on notation.** Some papers write $G_K^2$ for a different group, the maximal quotient of nilpotency class at most $2$ [@koymanspagano2024, §1.2]. That group is a quotient of the metabelian quotient defined here, since a group of class at most $2$ is metabelian.
